question: Does resampling whole customer trajectories provide useful uncertainty for fitted servicing policy values?
inherited: servicing-plan.json; same generated process and reward law
target: Value and improvement over no intervention for the policy selected on a separate training sample. Conditional on that independent selection, the evaluation target is fixed. This does not estimate the expected performance of a future retraining algorithm.
selection: Select among four thresholds on 2000 training trajectories using the existing known-law weighting comparison. Hold selected threshold fixed in all evaluation resamples. Record selection counts and finite-list regret.
estimation: Fit the Gaussian transition regression and residual standard deviation on observed evaluation transitions. Bootstrap 1000 entire initial-customer records with replacement; refit coefficients and residual variance on every draw. Observation patterns are resampled with each customer. Under baseline missing-at-random conditional on recorded state, no separate censoring model is needed for this conditional transition fit. Future-dependent dropout violates that assumption and is an adverse case, not repaired by bootstrap.
interval: 199 bootstrap draws; basic 95% interval [2*estimate-q.975,2*estimate-q.025] separately for value and improvement versus always-zero. Pair policy simulations within each draw. No finite-sample guarantee claimed.
integration: Fixed 2^13 scrambled Sobol normal trajectories for plug-in value integration, shared across estimates and resamples. Eight independent scrambles at the true parameter quantify integration sensitivity separately from parameter uncertainty. The generated initial law and reward are known, so their estimation uncertainty is excluded.
reference: 1,000,000 independent generated trajectories from separate seed; value, paired improvement and Monte Carlo SE retained for all policies. Coverage includes near-boundary reference uncertainty counts.
baselines: Known-law prefix IPW intervals on the same evaluation records and same selected policy; always-zero reward policy; fixed threshold .5. Plug-in g-computation without intervals is only the earlier point-estimate result.
criteria: Assess all-request coverage, Monte Carlo standard errors, width and paired lower-bound decisions. A systematic adverse-case failure rejects promotion under that assumption. No tuning after final outcomes. No method superiority from width alone.
review: Training and evaluation are independent; sampling unit is a whole trajectory. Selection uncertainty changes the target across independent replications and is accounted for by comparing with that selected policy's reference; reselecting inside evaluation-only bootstrap would answer a different question. Conditional outcome modeling does not estimate an inverse-censoring weight. Bootstrap cannot repair omitted predictors or future-dependent observation. Known initial and reward laws limit application. Integration sensitivity is checked before promoting interval claims.
stop: Stop affected study on singular fits, nonfinite values, missing resamples or exceeded budget. If integration sensitivity is material relative to statistical uncertainty, retain computation but classify the interval result inconclusive.
not_concluded: No universal post-selection confidence guarantee, no unobserved-outcome identification, no bank utility or ROI, no optimal policy or live model assessment.
